Subject: Kickoff: Performance acceptance and benchmark plan for ClearWater onboarding

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is the first-draft performance playbook for the ClearWater onboarding (clearwater-performance-playbook-v1.xlsx). High-level ask: we want to agree on the acceptance criteria and a ~2-day test window so we can hand off to Prod safely.

Proposed acceptance targets (initial):
- Latency: p95 <= 220 ms for typical request size (approx. 128 tokens)
- Median latency: <= 150 ms
- Sustained throughput: 400 req/min (steady-state, 5–10 min windows)
- Burst capacity: 800 req/min (1–2 minute windows)
- Error rate: < 0.5% 5xx or timeout

Planned test window: Jul 14–15 in staging (we can do staggered runs if you prefer). Deliverables from our side: k6 load script, test credentials, and a results CSV + quick analysis.

Please confirm: 1) Do these targets look reasonable to you? 2) Can your staging environment accept external load from our test harness (we can use an IP allowlist)? 3) Who from your side will be the technical lead during the run?

Cc'ing Laura (implementation lead) and Rachel (load engineer) to coordinate infra and measurement details.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—

Hi all —

We completed the main run this morning and I wanted to share the immediate findings before the retrospective. Raw CSV is attached (throughput-results-2026-07-14.csv). TL;DR: we hit sustained throughput but p95 latency missed the agreed target.

Summary highlights (Jul 14 run):
- Sustained throughput: 420 req/min (target 400 req/min) — PASS
- Burst capacity: 900 req/min achieved (target 800) — PASS
- Median latency: 172 ms — PASS
- p95 latency: 240 ms (target <= 220 ms) — FAIL (about 9% higher)
- Error rate: 0.18% 5xx/timeouts — PASS

Initial root cause notes:
- We observed a cold-KV-cache behavior when requests hit certain long-tail prefixes; p95 spikes correlate with cold-key churn.
- Default batch_size was 16 in the k6 script; increasing batch_size to 32 yields better throughput/latency in local repro.

Next steps proposed:
1) On Jul 15, run a tuned profile: pre-warm KV cache for 15 minutes, set batch_size=32, and repeat the sustained 3-hour run.
2) If p95 remains >220 ms after tuning, we will capture flamegraphs and thread dumps and schedule an engineering debug session (Vivek to lead).

Samira/Alex — are you available for the retest on Jul 15 (same window)? If yes, we'll proceed with the tuning and share updated CSV + short notes by EOD.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Load Engineer | Redwood Inference
